title: Anyone interested in making AI play games?
author: Empty_Attitude608
selftext:
I've seen recent researches on making AI play games. For example, Gemini 4 Argon playing Minecraft (tho I doubt that they are capable of playing in real-time).   
  
Would it be cool to make a game where your agent acts as a Pokemon, following the trainer (user) and combat with other Pokemons?  The Pokemon agent sees screen from their viewpoint. With proper prompts and tuning, do you think they can follow you and interact in real-time?   
  
What are some limitations, assuming using small local models like Gemma 4 E2B/E4B?

comments.author: weverz
comments.body: I find this topic to be a lot underrated

replies.author: Novaworld7
replies.body: Well it comes down to do you want it to learn how to play on its own or fire preloaded scripts based on inference.

replies.author: Empty_Attitude608
replies.body: An unpopular opinion is that scripting should be allowed as long as it relies purely on visual input rather than hidden game states (character coordinates or seeing through walls)? They can use scripts for object detection, which is AI-friendly

replies.author: Novaworld7
replies.body:
What I'm driving at is there's a lot of plumbing for this and a lot of it fakes or requires a tremendous amount of resources. I ran 2.5 K AI driven bots for a video game server. 

90% was just you are here, this is what's around you, what do you want to do, here are your options, this is your goal for right now. 

It's a pvp game as well so it had a lot of plumbing but it didn't feel AI driven. It felt like bots ... And a classifier basically. Yes they could talk and trade / fill orders fight you but it just felt like bots.

replies.author: Empty_Attitude608
replies.body:
Hosting smarter AI models on a server requires significant hardware resources. That's why I think a reasonable move is to let users train and bring their own AI. The game basically acts like a bridge.   
  
For example, a user and their AI could play soccer against another user and their AI, or users could play Pokémon with an AI partner by their side.

replies.author: Novaworld7
replies.body:
I am not sure what you are actually asking here. Though that would be just like permitting the AI to have an MCP into it and just using what the MCP exposes. More intelligent model or not...

Like I said, I brought in Haiku / Qwen 27b and 35B3A into the game and they played but they operated like bots, even with personas and all that jaz. The reason I say this is because when you give them a finite list of things they can do, they only operate within them. If you give them ultimate freedom sure... you can burn tokens having them learn what to do but there are better uses out there for it.

comments.author: Templeshooter
comments.body: I trained a model to play pokemon vgc doubles, it beats most human opponents. Training took about 24 hours on rtx 4090. The model is like 2.7M parameters, it is like 20 megabytes on disk, and inference takes like 2 ms on cpu per turn.

replies.author: Empty_Attitude608
replies.body:
congrats on getting your AI smart and efficient!  
is this AI already hosted in your server that plays against most human opponents? do you see yourself train AI for different games (assume you are having fun with it)?

replies.author: Templeshooter
replies.body:
I ran it on my home lab server, and I let it climb the ladder on pokemon showdown, but then I decided to stop as I have proven to myself that ai model can play competitively, and I didnt want to annoy players. but after that admins of pokemon showdown added a bot account mode, you can register as bot and go wild, but real players can opt out from bot matches.

I am currently vibe coding a mmo just for fun (never expect it to get any players, it was just a long time dream of mine) and i had this idea to train transformers to act as like, boss ai or bot opponents in "pvp" arena, like wow's comp stomp. but to train on self play, you got to make a simulator that would resolve matches very quickjly; my pokemon simulator could do like 20000 games per second

comments.author: Stinky_You
comments.body: Too much usage for me. But I got Claude to give itself abilities for godot.

replies.author: Empty_Attitude608
replies.body:
yeh, it might not be a well-spent using big LLMs.

For experiments, I tried to let gpt 6-Astra play games, it is slow even after I expose an API to move. Claude simply writes scripts to handle it, but for a total different scenario, it breaks.

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
umm, they are playing it in real-time... they just don't process visuals fast enough so they don't do well in some games.

can small local models "see" the screen now? because the frontier models can

replies.author: Empty_Attitude608
replies.body:
There are quite a few multimodal models that you can run on your own GPU. Gemma 4 is one of them; it can accept text, vision, and audio, and output texts. 

[HuggingFace AnyToAny Models under 12B](https://huggingface.co/models?pipeline_tag=any-to-any&num_parameters=min:0,max:12B&sort=trending)

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
AIs can accept vision inputs since a long time ago. that is not the issue.

Playing a game requires the AI to constantly receive vision inputs on its own, provide inputs to control the game, rinse and repeat

I know that frontier models can because I have been asking them to do simple playtests since last month

if you can make it work with local models, then more power to you

comments.author: SolrayCultist
comments.body: The AI Trackmania community is insanely fun to watch.
